run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The only fault the retained evidence shows is in the tracing backend of the social-network namespace: the Deployment jaeger was re-created out-of-band (kubectl-client-side-apply at 2026-11-24T03:51:39Z, whereas every other app Deployment in social-network was created by helm at 03:51:31Z) with 2 replicas, a single ReadWriteOnce openebs-hostpath claim (jaeger-pvc, PV pinned by nodeAffinity to sregym-worker3) and a required podAntiAffinity on kubernetes.io/hostname. The single RWO volume plus the hard hostname anti-affinity make the second replica permanently unschedulable: pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-2bj4t is Pending/Unschedulable with '1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules ... 2 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict', while the one running replica sits on the very node the PV is pinned to. Prometheus alert rules PendingPodsDetected and PodSchedulingFailure for that pod are firing. The social-network request path itself showed no fault in the sampled window: all other 26 Deployments are 1/1 ready/available with 0 restarts, every Service has endpoints, 30 traces (103 spans, 12 services) between 03:51:40Z and 03:51:55Z show zero error rows and HTTP 200 on /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read, a full compose trace shows every downstream Thrift/Mongo/Redis call present and successful, and logs contain only MongoDB index-creation retries during pod startup plus expected 'user_id ... not found' warnings from an empty social graph. The conclusion is partial because the environment was recreated minutes before the window end: Prometheus holds a single scrape (2026-11-24T03:51:56Z) and Loki/Jaeger retain nothing before ~03:51:3x, so no baseline, trend, or pre-incident state exists, the register/follow/unfollow paths were never exercised, and the change_history integration is not available to show who applied the jaeger manifest or why.

claims.text: Deployment jaeger (namespace social-network) exists with metadata.creationTimestamp 2026-11-24T03:51:39Z and generation 1, and its only non-status manager is kubectl-client-side-apply at 2026-11-24T03:51:39Z.

All 26 other social-network Deployments (compose-post-service, home-timeline-*, media-*, nginx-thrift, post-storage-*, social-graph-*, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-*, user-*, user-mention-service) were created at 2026-11-24T03:51:31Z with helm as manager, so jaeger was created separately, 8 seconds later, by a different writer.

Deployment jaeger spec has spec.replicas=2, volumes jaeger-config (config source, no claim) and jaeger-volume backed by persistentVolumeClaim jaeger-pvc, and spec.template.spec.affinity.podAntiAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution with topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname selecting label service In (jaeger).

PersistentVolumeClaim jaeger-pvc is Bound with accessMode ReadWriteOnce, storageClass openebs-hostpath, volumeName pvc-faeb11cf-145a-462e-9e0d-bbfaf75187ce; that PV has required nodeAffinity kubernetes.io/hostname In (sregym-worker3) and path /var/openebs/local/pvc-faeb11cf-145a-462e-9e0d-bbfaf75187ce.

Pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-2bj4t is Pending and Unschedulable (PodScheduled=False, reason Unschedulable) with message '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 2 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict'; the ReplicaSet event records the same FailedScheduling ('2 node(s) didn't find available persistent volumes to bind' at 03:51:41Z, then '2 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict' at 03:51:43Z).

The only running jaeger replica, pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-bfdls, is scheduled on node sregym-worker3 - the same node the jaeger-pvc PersistentVolume is pinned to by nodeAffinity - and is Ready with 0 restarts, while jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-2bj4t has no node assigned at 03:54:52Z.
Deployment jaeger reports spec.replicas=2 with readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1 and unavailableReplicas=1, i.e. it stays one replica short of its desired count.

Alert rules in the loaded Prometheus report PendingPodsDetected and PodSchedulingFailure firing (state firing, severity critical) for pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-2bj4t in namespace social-network at lastEvaluation 2026-11-24T03:53:09Z, and DeploymentNotReady pending for deployment jaeger with value 0.

All social-network application microservice pods are Running and ready with 0 restarts (28 pods listed, only jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-2bj4t Pending), and every social-network application Deployment is available/ready 1 of 1 except jaeger.

All 26 ClusterIP Services in social-network have non-empty Endpoints (e.g. nginx-thrift 10.244.7.254:8080, compose-post-service 10.244.7.250:9090, user-timeline-service 10.244.234.161:9090), so no Service selector/port mismatch is visible.

30 traces of nginx-web-server covering 103 spans across 12 services between 2026-11-24T03:51:40.469Z and 03:51:55.653Z contain 0 error rows; the nginx server spans /wrk2-api/post/compose (2), /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read (14) and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read (8) all carry http.status_code=200 with durations of 0.8-8.1 ms.

Whole trace 00c440476d9cb8f3 (33 spans, 2026-11-24T03:51:40Z) shows the complete compose path - nginx-web-server -> compose-post-service -> text-service (url-shorten-service, user-mention-service) / user-service / media-service / unique-id-service / post-storage-service / home-timeline-service -> social-graph-service, user-timeline-service - with no error status and no missing parent-child links in the returned data; user-service compose_creator_server returned in 8 us with no child spans, which is the only span shape that differs from its peers.

A case-insensitive Loki scan of all social-network container logs in the window for error|fail|exception|panic|refused|timeout|timed out returned only 28 lines, all MongoDB index-creation retries logged while pods were starting (03:51:33Z-03:51:36Z, e.g. 'Failed to create mongodb index, try again' / 'No suitable servers found ... user-mongodb:27017'); no runtime error, exception or timeout line from any service was returned.

social-graph-service logs repeated normal-priority warnings 'GetFollowers) user_id: <n> not found' at a high rate (60 lines in 03:51:51-03:51:55Z of 169 in-window lines, 1628 further lines after the window), consistent with reads against an empty graph store rather than a service error.

All 17 service-config.json ConfigMaps in social-network resolve to one identical dependency addr/port signature (single group of 17: compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, jaeger, media-frontend, media-memcached, media-service, post-storage-memcached, post-storage-service, social-graph-service, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-memcached, url-shorten-service, user-memcached, user-mention-service, user-service, user-timeline-service), so no service is configured with a divergent dependency address or port.

Namespace social-network contains no ResourceQuota and no NetworkPolicy objects, and all four nodes (sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3) are Ready=True with DiskPressure=False, so the jaeger scheduling failure is not caused by quota or node pressure.

The kube-state-metrics snapshot at 2026-11-24T03:51:56Z is inconsistent/stale mid-rollout - it reports kube_pod_status_phase Running=1 for the already-deleted pod jaeger-7d8548779-gkggb and both Pending=1 and Running=1 for jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-bfdls, and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="jaeger"}=0 - so that single scrape's '0 available' value is not used as the current replica count; the Deployment object itself reported 1 ready/1 available of 2 at 03:52:05Z.

Because the RWO PV is pinned to sregym-worker3 and the Deployment requires hostname-spread anti-affinity, the second jaeger replica can never be placed while both settings stand; only removing one of them (replicas=1, per-replica storage, or a soft/non-required anti-affinity) would let it schedule.

The jaeger re-creation by kubectl-client-side-apply at 03:51:39Z (new object, replicas 2 plus a new RWO claim, replacing the helm-created single-replica jaeger whose pod jaeger-7d8548779-gkggb was killed at 03:51:39Z) is the change that introduced the unschedulable replica; whether it was an intentional fault injection or a bootstrap step cannot be determined without the missing change_history integration.

Rejected: a failing social-network microservice (error/timeout in compose-post-service, text-service, user-service, user-mention-service, url-shorten-service, post-storage-service, home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service, social-graph-service, media-service, unique-id-service or nginx-web-server). Every such Deployment is 1/1 ready/available with 0 restarts, the sampled traces show 0 error rows and HTTP 200 on all exercised endpoints, and no runtime error, exception or timeout log line was found in the window.

Rejected: misdirected service configuration or missing endpoints between social-network services. The dependency address/port signature of all 17 service-config.json ConfigMaps is identical and every ClusterIP Service has endpoints.

Make Deployment jaeger schedulable: set replicas=1, or give each replica its own volume (or RWX storage) and/or use preferredDuringScheduling (soft) hostname anti-affinity instead of requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution; until then the jaeger Deployment will keep alerting with one permanently Pending replica.

gaps: The whole cluster is minutes old at the window end (all Deployments created by helm at 2026-11-24T03:51:31Z; Loki returned no lines for 2026-11-24T02:30:00Z-03:45:00Z; Jaeger restarted at 03:51:44Z and holds only traces from 03:51:40Z on), so no pre-incident state, restart history or change record exists for the outage question.

Prometheus exposes only a single sample per series at 2026-11-24T03:51:56Z (node_load1 and sum(probe_success{job="blackbox-social-network"}) each returned one point over a 24h range), so rate/increase-based error-rate and latency comparisons and any latency trend versus a baseline are unavailable; missing ERROR series must be treated as unknown, not zero.

Whether the jaeger Deployment change was an injected fault or a bootstrap step is unknown: the change_history integration is not available in this Run and secrets cannot be read, so the intent and any accompanying manifest/values details could not be verified.

No trace or log evidence covers /wrk2-api/user/register, /wrk2-api/user/follow, /wrk2-api/user/unfollow or /wrk2-api/user/get_follower; nginx-web-server operations seen since the Jaeger restart are only /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read, /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read, ReadUserTimeline, compose_post_client and read_home_timeline_client, so those paths remain unchecked.

Redis-level evidence is missing: redis_info returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so home-timeline-redis, social-graph-redis and user-timeline-redis memory, eviction and persistence state could not be checked (only their client spans, which succeeded at 23-279 us).

The scale of user-facing impact of the single jaeger replica is unverified: no application error or latency evidence ties the pending jaeger pod to any request failure, and the effect of losing one of two tracing backends on ingestion or query reliability was not measured.

Kubernetes objects are the state at query time (03:51:58Z-03:54:52Z), so pod-phase/kube-state-metrics values such as the transient jaeger available=0 at 03:51:56Z cannot establish what was true earlier in the 24h window.
next_steps: Review the jaeger manifest/values that were applied with kubectl-client-side-apply at 2026-11-24T03:51:39Z (2 replicas, jaeger-pvc RWO openebs-hostpath) to decide between replicas=1, per-replica storage, or soft anti-affinity.

Once more than one Prometheus scrape exists, re-check error rate and p95 latency per service_name (traces_span_metrics_calls_total with status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR", traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket) against a pre-change baseline.
Exercise the register/follow/unfollow/get_follower endpoints or inspect their spans after the load generator covers them, to confirm the untested write paths of user-service and social-graph-service.
Check the three Redis backends (home-timeline-redis, social-graph-redis, user-timeline-redis) for maxmemory, evictions and persistence once a read-only Redis connection is available.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.span_groups_note: span_groups summarizes the spans shown in content; spans the adapter sampled out are not counted in any group.
